Propensity model sensitivity of a matched design

Source: R/propensity_sensitivity.R
propensity_sensitivity.Rd

How much does a matched design depend on which of several similarly good propensity models is used? The function refits the propensity model with every algorithm of the model set, repeats the analyst's matching with each model, keeps the models that pass a quality gate (the kept models), and describes how much the kept models disagree. No outcome is used.

Usage

propensity_sensitivity(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "bart", "grf_probability"),
  seeds = 1:3,
  folds = 5,
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  n_trees = NULL,
  quality_tolerance = 0.05,
  balance_rule = c("relative", "absolute", "relative_only"),
  balance_margin = 0.1,
  balance_cap = 0.25,
  balance_threshold = 0.1,
  bootstrap_samples = 20,
  covariates = NULL,
  replace = FALSE,
  m_order = "largest",
  caliper = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1,
  min_treated_kept = NULL,
  clip_bootstrap = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.propensity_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A matchit object (from MatchIt::matchit()) or a two-sided formula such as treat ~ x1 + x2. Only baseline covariates belong in the formula; exclude outcomes, identifiers and post-treatment variables (for example, treat ~ . - death - id). The treatment may be numeric 0/1, logical or a two-level factor (see fit_propensity_models()).

data

The data frame. Required with a formula; with a matchit object it is looked up from the object's call when NULL.

algorithms

The propensity model set. The default is logistic regression, BART and the GRF probability forest (with the default seeds, three seeds for each tree algorithm: seven models; packages 'dbarts' and 'grf'). A faster set is available with algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting") (packages 'randomForest' and 'gbm'); it has been studied less. See fit_propensity_models() for every option and the fixed settings.

seeds

1:k, the number of seeds per tree algorithm (default 1:3). Only the number is used; set the randomness with seed.

folds, cross_fit, n_trees, quality_tolerance

Passed to fit_propensity_models(). n_trees applies to gradient boosting only.

balance_rule

The balance part of the quality gate: "relative" (default), "relative_only" (the relative rule without the cap) or "absolute". See Steps.

balance_margin, balance_cap

Relative rule: a model fails if its post-match maximum absolute standardized mean difference on main terms is more than balance_margin above the best model's (default 0.10) or above balance_cap (default 0.25; not used by "relative_only").

balance_threshold

Absolute rule: largest allowed post-match maximum absolute standardized mean difference on main terms (default 0.10). Used only with balance_rule = "absolute".

bootstrap_samples

Number of logistic bootstrap refits, for the bootstrap rank instability and the bootstrap pair recurrence: 0 for none, otherwise at least 2 (default 20).

covariates

Data frame of covariates for the control spread and the balance statistics. Its rows must be the same patients in the same order as data; when both have row names other than the default and they differ, the function stops. NULL (default) uses the source columns of the formula's right-hand side, from data, resolved with R's formula rules: . means every other column and exclusions such as - death are respected; I(age^2) gives age, age:diabetes gives age and diabetes. Character columns are an error (convert them to factors).

replace, m_order, caliper

Matching options for the formula interface (without replacement, order "largest", no caliper by default; the caliper is in standard deviations of each model's logit). With a matchit object they are read from the object and must not be given.

cores

Number of cores (default 1). Run time grows with the number of patients and covariates (about a minute for 614 patients and 7 covariates; about 16 minutes for 5,735 patients and 50 covariates on one core); on Unix, cores runs the models in parallel.

seed

Integer seed from which every other seed is derived (fold split, models, bootstrap). See the section "Seeds".

min_treated_kept

NULL (default, off) or a share between 0 and 1: with a caliper, a model that keeps a smaller share of the treated patients fails the quality gate and is left out before the relative balance limit is computed.

clip_bootstrap

FALSE (default) or TRUE: clip the bootstrap refits' scores to [0.001, 0.999] as the cross-fitted scores are. The default keeps the method as it was studied; see match_each_model().

digits

Significant digits for printed numbers.

...

Not used.

object

A propensity_sensitivity object.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

Value

An object of class "propensity_sensitivity": a list with

  • patients: one row per patient (id, treated, rank_disagreement, rank_disagreement_between, rank_disagreement_within, logit_disagreement, control_spread, control_spread_scaled, pair_recurrence_models, pair_recurrence_bootstrap, outside_support, logistic_score; the treated-only measures are NA for untreated patients). These columns describe the spread over patients; they are not per-patient flags.

  • models: one row per model (fit, balance, treated_kept, the gate columns, in_use = kept, gate_note), plus the row of your own model for a matchit object.

  • summary: a list with table (the study-level numbers with the gate, with_gate, and without it, without_gate), quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models, reference_model_not_kept, models_used (the kept models), kept_algorithms, kept_algorithms_count, kept_models_one_algorithm, pair_recurrence_floor_models, pair_instability_maximum and pair_recurrence_expected_ceiling_bootstrap_uncorrected.

  • quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models and kept_algorithms_count (also at the top level, for scripts).

  • balance_spread: spread tables with and without the gate.

  • bootstrap_rank_instability: see bootstrap_rank_instability(); NULL without bootstrap refits.

  • settings and components (model_set, the fitted fit_propensity_models() object with every model's cross-fitted probability, logit and rank, so that the scores can be reused without refitting; and match_set).

Details

Every summary is study-level: read it for the study as a whole. Rank disagreement is the primary summary. Pair instability, rank disagreement with equal weight per algorithm and the between/within-algorithm ratio are exploratory. Bootstrap rank instability, balance spread and control spread are descriptive. The per-patient columns of patients (and of as.data.frame()) describe how the disagreement is spread over the patients; they are not flags for individual patients. No thresholds for a "large" value exist yet.

These diagnostics have been studied in the author's simulations and benchmark analyses; a methods paper is in preparation. No peer-reviewed evaluation exists yet.

Two situations raise an R warning and a block in print() and summary(): fewer than two models pass the quality gate (every model is then used, so there is no set of similarly good models to compare), and the kept models are seeds of a single algorithm (rank disagreement and pair instability then measure seed noise within that algorithm).

Steps

  1. All arguments, the treatment and the covariates are checked before any model is fitted.

  2. fit_propensity_models() with the formula (cross-fitted scores by default).

  3. match_each_model() with the matching options and the logistic bootstrap block.

  4. balance_spread() for every model.

  5. Quality gate: passed_quality_gate = passed_logloss_gate & smd_max_main <= balance_limit. With the default balance_rule = "relative" the limit is the smallest max |SMD| on main terms among the refitted models plus balance_margin (0.10), and never above balance_cap (0.25): a model is excluded only when its balance is clearly worse than the best model's. With balance_rule = "relative_only" the limit is the best model's value plus balance_margin, without the cap; use it as a sensitivity analysis when the cap excludes every model (many covariates). With balance_rule = "absolute" the limit is balance_threshold (0.10). With min_treated_kept set (off by default), a model that keeps a smaller share of the treated patients fails the gate and does not enter the best-model value of the relative rule. If fewer than two models pass, every model is used and quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models is TRUE.

  6. rank_disagreement(), control_spread(), pair_recurrence() and the balance spread on the kept models (summary column with_gate) and on every model (without_gate).

Seeds

The fold split and every tree model depend on seed. On small data the kept models and every summary can change noticeably with seed (on lalonde, rank disagreement varied several-fold between seeds). Rerun with two or three values of seed and report all of them; seed_sensitivity() does this. Rank disagreement is a standard deviation over the kept models, so it also depends on how many seeds each kept algorithm contributes; "rank disagreement, equal weight per algorithm" counts each algorithm once.

What the summaries compare under a caliper

With a caliper each model keeps a different subset of the treated patients, shown by print() for each kept model. The standardized mean differences compare the matched treated patients with their matched untreated partners; the energy distance (cobalt::bal.init(estimand = "ATT")) also measures the distance to the whole treated group, so it also grows when treated patients are dropped. Rank disagreement averages over all treated patients, matched or not; pair instability and control spread use the treated patients matched by at least one kept model. The gate does not look at the share of treated kept unless min_treated_kept is set: a model that keeps few treated patients can reach an easy balance and then set the relative limit for the others.

Estimand

Matching is 1:1 nearest-neighbour on the logit of each model's score, for the average treatment effect in the treated (ATT). Without replacement (the default of the formula interface and the more common applied choice) the result depends on the matching order, and late matches can be poor when untreated patients are not much more numerous than treated ones, so the matched estimate can keep some bias for the ATT. With replacement every treated patient gets its nearest untreated patient; under overlap and a correctly specified propensity model this targets the ATT, at the price of reused untreated patients and a variance that must account for it. With a caliper, treated patients without an eligible partner are dropped and the estimand is the effect in the retained treated patients, not the ATT.

Reading a matchit object

From a matchit object the function reads the formula, the method, ratio, replace, m.order (from the call; MatchIt's default for the ATT with a propensity score is "largest") and the caliper. Only 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on a propensity score for the ATT is supported, with or without replacement and with or without a caliper on the score; anything else (including exact, mahvars, antiexact, s.weights, reuse.max, unit.id and calipers on covariates) stops with a clear error. MatchIt applies a caliper in standard deviations of the analyst's distance (over all patients); the same number of standard deviations is applied to the logit of every model here. When data is NULL the data is found by evaluating the object's data argument in the calling frame.

Your own model

The analyst's own score (x$distance) is kept as an extra row of models with model_id = "reference". Its ranks come from x$distance (ranks do not depend on the scale) and its balance statistics from x$weights. Its log-loss, Brier score and c-statistic are NA: it is an in-sample score from the user's object and is not comparable with the cross-fitted scores. It is judged on balance only, as "within the balance limit" or "above the balance limit"; it is never one of the models compared, so it is never "kept". summary reports its mean absolute rank difference from the kept models, over treated patients: the mean over treated i and models m of |r_ref(i) - r_m(i)|.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
                            data = lalonde, distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit",
                            replace = TRUE)
# A fast model set for this example; the default set is slower (see below).
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(
  matched, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  seeds = 1, n_trees = 100, bootstrap_samples = 5
)
#> Warning: Fewer than two models passed the quality gate, so there is no set of similarly good models to compare. Every model is used below; read the values as a description of all models, not of a kept set.
sensitivity
